author: evangelink
body:
## Why

The code-testing-* agent family in the `dotnet-test` plugin generates tests for **12 languages** (not just .NET — see `code-testing-extensions/extensions/{dotnet,python,typescript,powershell,cpp,go,java,rust,ruby,swift,kotlin}.md` + `dotnet-examples.md`). However, nothing in the implementer prompt tells it to keep changes additive. In practice it routinely:

- modifies existing test files non-additively (deletes/reformats lines), and
- edits non-test production code to make something easier to test.

Both behaviors are rejected by:

- the msbench `simple` test verifier (any `dels > 0` on a test file, or any change to a non-test file, sets `reward=0`);
- most real-world test-quality gates and code-review policies (this is what the `testability-migration` agent exists for).

In a recent msbench comparison (vanilla `github-copilot-cli` vs. `cta-dotnet-all` with all `dotnet/skills` plugins enabled), the skill-enabled run regressed on 26 tasks where vanilla passed. After excluding tasks where a separate runner bug hid the agent's commits, ~8 of the remaining regressions trace directly back to destructive edits on test files or to edits of non-test source files — exactly what these rules forbid.

## What

Add a short `Edit boundaries (cross-language invariants)` subsection to Step 4 of `code-testing-implementer.agent.md`, plus a single corresponding entry in the `Rules` section:

1. **Existing test files are append-only.** No reformat/reorder/rename/remove. Even whitespace-only churn counts as destructive.
2. **Do not modify non-test source files.** Surface untestable seams as follow-ups for the `testability-migration` agent.
3. **Prefer new test files over edits to existing ones** when both options are valid.
4. **One exception**: build-system manifests (`.csproj`/`.sln`/`pom.xml`/`build.gradle`/`Cargo.toml`/`package.json`/etc.) may be edited only for project/dependency registration.

Total change: `+10 / -0` in a single file. No behavioral change to skills or other agents.

## Why the implementer agent specifically

The implementer is the only agent in the pipeline that writes test files. The orchestrator (`code-testing-generator`) and the upstream agents (`researcher`, `planner`) don't author code. Putting the invariants where the file edits actually happen keeps the rule close to the action.

author: blackeagle54
body:
## Issue #25 — Spellcasting crashes with `canCast` undefined (case-sensitive class lookup)

Casting in combat crashed with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'canCast')`. `character.characterClass` is a **free-form string** (schema default `'fighter'`) and is commonly stored capitalized (e.g. `"Cleric"`), but `SPELLCASTING_CONFIG` keys are lowercase. Seven validator functions indexed the config with the raw class and no null check, so a capitalized **or** custom class produced `undefined` → crash on the next property access.

## Fix
Route all seven through the **existing** `getSpellcastingConfig()` helper, which already lowercases and returns a safe non-caster default for unknown classes — the same pattern `canCastSpells`/`characterKnowsSpell`/`restoreAllSpellSlots`/`restorePactSlots` already used:

- `getMaxSpellLevel`, `getInitialSpellSlots`, `calculateSpellSaveDC`, `calculateSpellAttackBonus`, `hasSpellSlotAvailable`, `validateSpellCast`, `consumeSpellSlot`

This fixes both the capitalization bug **and** unknown/custom-class crashes (monsters/NPCs), and removes now-redundant unsafe dereferences — DRY with the code that already worked.

## Tests (RED → GREEN)
New `tests/engine/magic/spell-validator.test.ts`: a capitalized `"Cleric"` computes the correct save DC (15), attack bonus (+7), max spell level, and slot availability; a custom class (`"Chronomancer"`) is treated as a non-caster instead of crashing. The 74 existing `spellcasting.test.ts` cases (all lowercase classes) remain green. Full suite **2001 passing**, `tsc --noEmit` clean.

### Why it wasn't caught before
Every existing spellcasting test used lowercase class strings (`'cleric'`, `'wizard'`), so the capitalized-class path was never exercised.

author: benzsevern
body:
## Summary
The BODS ingest (`src/shellnet/sources/bods.py`) emitted persons and entities but **dropped the person→company PSC relationship layer**. As a result, a sanctioned-PSC match in the survivor pipeline (keyed by `uk_psc:<statementId>`) couldn't be resolved to the company it controls without re-parsing the 3.5 GB `uk_bods.zip` by hand (exactly what was needed in PR #152 to name the oligarchs' companies).

This adds `_build_uk_psc_relationships` and wires it into `ingest()` to persist **`uk_psc_relationships.parquet`**.

## How it works
- Reads `relationship_statement` (`recordDetails_subject` = controlled company `GB-COH-<n>`, `recordDetails_interestedParty` = person `recordId`), drops component sub-statements.
- Joins the `relationship_recorddetails_interests` sub-table for nature-of-control (`type`), `directOrIndirect`, share band (`share_min`/`share_max`), and dates.
- Joins `person_statement` to map the person `recordId` → `statementId`.

Emitted columns: `source, person_source_id, person_record_id, company_id, company_number, control_type, direct_or_indirect, share_min, share_max, start_date, end_date`.

`person_source_id` is the BODS `statementId` — exactly the `uk_psc:<id>` key the unified person table emits, so a survivor match joins straight onto this edge. `company_number` is prefix-stripped/normalized to align with `uk_psc_entities.company_number`.

## Validation
- New tests in `tests/test_bods_uk_psc_relationships.py` (4) + full suite green; ruff check + format clean.
- Run against the **real** corpus: **13,108,403 edges**; the five sanctioned oligarchs from PR #152 resolve correctly (e.g. Marchenko → GB-COH-04445610, shareholding 75–100%; Mordashov → GB-COH-13287342, shareholding 25–50%). ~7% of edges have a null `person_source_id` — these are corporate-PSC (parent-company) controllers, which is expected.

## Deploy note
No new job-server allowlist entry needed; the existing `ingest_uk_bods` script now also writes this parquet. Requires a Railway redeploy + re-run of `ingest_uk_bods` to materialize it on the volume.

## Test plan
- [ ] CI green (pytest + ruff)
- [ ] After deploy: re-run `ingest_uk_bods`, confirm `interim/uk_psc_relationships.parquet` lands and joins to the survivor matches

author: glslang
body:
## Problem

`load_config` errored on a missing `AGENT_NOTIFY_TOKEN` **before** `main()` applied the `--token`/`--server` CLI flags. So when there was no `bridge.toml` and no env var, passing the flags alone could not start the bridge:

```
$ agent-notify-bridge --server http://host:8787 --token secret
Error: set AGENT_NOTIFY_TOKEN or create bridge.toml at one of: ...
```

The flags were applied only after the load already failed.

## Fix

Defer the requirement check until the config layers are merged:

- **`load_config`** returns an empty token instead of erroring when `AGENT_NOTIFY_TOKEN` is unset, so CLI flags can still supply it.
- **`BridgeConfig::token`** is now `#[serde(default)]`, so a `bridge.toml` may set `server_url` and leave the token to `--token`/the env var.
- New **`settings::validate()`** checks the fully-merged config (file/env + CLI overrides) and is called from `main()` after the overrides are applied. A token from *any* layer now satisfies the requirement, and the error message lists all three sources.

Precedence is unchanged: CLI flags override the file/env base.

## Tests

New unit tests in `settings.rs`:
- `validate` accepts a complete config and rejects a blank token / blank server (with the expected messages).
- `cli_token_bootstraps_base_without_token` — mirrors `main()`: an empty-token base (as from the env path with no `AGENT_NOTIFY_TOKEN`) fails, then validates once a `--token` override is applied.
- `read_config` parses a file that omits the token (defaulted) and a fully-populated file.

`cargo fmt --check`, workspace `clippy -D warnings`, and `cargo test` all pass.

End-to-end: with no `bridge.toml` and no env vars, `agent-notify-bridge --server ... --token ... --mock-display` now boots into the tray + worker connect loop instead of erroring on a missing token.

author: febaemanuel
body:
## Continuação do PR #171 (já mergeado)

Ajustes do relatório estatístico SCIH pro contexto específico da Maternidade Escola Assis Chateaubriand (MEAC).

## O que mudou

### 1. Régua de N calibrada pra realidade da MEAC

Em vez dos cortes acadêmicos genéricos (10/30/100/300), usar limiares baseados no fluxo real de cesáreas/mês da MEAC e taxa típica de resposta WhatsApp (~40%):

| N respondidos | Confiabilidade | O que dá pra fazer |
|---|---|---|
| < 20 | ❌ Insuficiente | Acumular mais dados |
| 20-50 | ⚠️ Tendência | Comparar com histórico, não subgrupos |
| 50-150 | 🟡 Análise mensal | Estimar prevalência mensal |
| 150-500 | ✅ Análise trimestral | Comparar subgrupos |
| > 500 | ✅ Vigilância robusta | Modelo multivariado, NNIS |

### 2. Badge dinâmico atualizado
Aparece no cabeçalho ao lado de "Respondidos: 31" → `⚠️ N tendência`. Categoriza visualmente conforme a nova régua.

### 3. Alertas automáticos recalibrados
- `N<20` → alerta vermelho (insuficiente)
- `N<50` → alerta amarelo (tratar como tendência)

### 4. Bloco novo "Contexto ANVISA"

Explica o que o questionário SCIH **cobre vs não cobre** com base na classificação oficial de ISC:

- **ISC Incisional Superficial** (até 30d): ✅ Bem coberta (sinais flogísticos diretos)
- **ISC Incisional Profunda** (até 30-90d): 🟡 Parcialmente coberta (febre + sintomas gerais)
- **ISC Órgão/Espaço** (até 30-90d): ❌ Não coberta (precisa exame/imagem)

Inclui recomendação ANVISA/CDC NHSN sobre vigilância em 30 dias (cesárea) e 90 dias (mastologia com prótese), e sugestão de enviar em D+7 e D+30 pra ampliar cobertura temporal.

## Sem migration

Só template + ajuste de threshold em Python. Nenhuma alteração de schema.

## Deploy

```bash
cd ~/busca
git fetch origin && git checkout master && git pull origin master
docker compose up -d --build web
```

## Test plan

- [ ] Abrir `/scih/relatorio-estatistico` com a campanha 4 selecionada
- [ ] Verificar que o badge ao lado de "Respondidos: 31" agora mostra `⚠️ N tendência` (não mais "N razoável")
- [ ] Verificar que o alerta amarelo apareceu (N entre 20-50)
- [ ] Abrir a seção "Como ler este relatório" e verificar a nova tabela calibrada pra MEAC
- [ ] Verificar o novo bloco "Contexto ANVISA" com os 3 níveis de ISC

author: elementalcollision
body:
## Summary

Operator-fired respike of PR #75's redesigned `_extract_user_context` against the 30 oracle single-session-preference items. **Gate A PASS** (3/16 wrong→right), **Gate B FAIL by 1** (1 regression, threshold 0). Net delta +6.67pp; dramatic improvement over v1 (5→1 regressions), but binary gate is binary.

## Gates

| Gate | Threshold | v1 (PR #73) | v2 (this respike) |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| A | ≥2/16 | 3 (PASS) | **3 (PASS)** |
| B | =0/14 | 5 (FAIL) | **1 (FAIL by 1)** |
| Regression check | ≥2/3 v1 flips | n/a | **1/3 (FAIL)** |

## Key insight

The single Gate B failure (`d6233ab6` — nostalgic, high school reunion) is the **same item** that regressed in v1's noisy heuristic. v1's hypothesis on `d6233ab6` and v2's hypothesis differ in content but both miss the gold direction. The pre-intervention baseline was lucky-correct: surfacing ANY user context — noisy or clean — gives the answerer enough confidence to commit to the wrong direction.

If `d6233ab6` is excluded as a known intrinsic outlier (same regression in both heuristics), the redesigned spike is **0/14 right→wrong**. But the pre-registered gate doesn't have an outlier-exclusion mechanism; strict reading is FAIL.

## Decision tension

Pre-registered gates were binary by design — the point of pre-registration is to bind the decision. But:

- v1 had 5 regressions across diverse items → broad noise
- v2 has 1 regression on a known-sensitive item → narrow signal

The framework caught this difference cleanly (binary threshold fails both, but the count delta is huge). The question is whether the framework's strictness or the underlying win/loss ratio improvement should drive the decision.

## Three operator paths

1. **Honor strict gates → Option C** (revert PR #75, declare out-of-reach, release on 90.80%). Defensible. The pre-registered framework was load-bearing.
2. **Adjusted reading → accept the trade.** Risk: relaxing pre-registered gates sets a precedent.
3. **Hybrid → Path 3 (recommended).** Keep PR #75 as **Proposed**; run a full $2 corpus sweep to convert ambiguous n=30 evidence into n=500 signal. If corpus ≥90.80% AND SPP ≥50%, accept and flip ADR 0138 to Accepted. Otherwise revert.

## What's in this PR

One file: `mind/research/implicit-preference-respike-result-2026-05-25.md` (~150 lines).

- Paired-item flip table (3 wins, 1 loss vs v1's 3/5)
- Side-by-side v1 vs v2 comparison
- Per-item diagnostic on `d6233ab6` (the persistent regressor)
- McNemar's-test sample-size honesty (p≈0.32 at n=30; +6.67pp not significant in aggregate)
- Three operator paths with explicit cost + tradeoff per path
- Spike-protocol meta-note (suggests discordant-pair tests + known-outlier mechanisms for future ADR-0138-style chips)

## Charter discipline

- No code change, no test change, no ADR amend (status flip / revert decision pending operator)
- Operator decides between Paths 1/2/3
- Cost matches spike budget (~$0.05)
- Honest disclosure: McNemar's-test p ≈ 0.32 at n=30; the load-bearing measurement is the win/loss ratio change (3:5 → 3:1), not aggregate accuracy

🤖 Operator-run spike; deliverable is the result note.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

This PR enables nightly CI testing for the OpenShift LVM operator against OCP 4.23 releases by adding a new Prow job configuration.

**What's being changed:**
A new CI configuration file (`openshift-lvm-operator-main__4.23-nightly.yaml`) is added to define nightly build and test jobs for the LVM operator. The openshift/lvm-operator repository does not have a release-4.23 branch; both 4.23 and 5.0 versions build from the main branch. This configuration enables the proper testing setup for the 4.23 release.

The configuration defines multiple integration test jobs covering:
- AWS Single-Node and Multi-Node clusters (x86-64 and ARM64 architectures)
- EquinixMetal bare metal SNO/MNO dualstack configurations

All tests use the OCP 4.23 RHEL9 base image and run the LVM operator's integration test suite against the corresponding cluster configurations.

## Summary
Closes recipe-pool backlog area **A**: turns the planner/cross-journey `@pending` E2E scenarios green against the real recipe pool — and in doing so **the E2E suite found a genuine latent product bug**, fixed here.

### The bug (found by the new E2E)
`PlanPersister` grouped meal slots into `Day` rows by `SlotAssignment.dayId()`, but `planner_days` is `UNIQUE(plan_id, on_date)`. The slot skeleton mints a **distinct `dayId` per slot kind**, so any real **multi-kind day** (breakfast/lunch/dinner/snack on one date) produced multiple `Day` rows with the same `on_date` → `23505` duplicate-key → **HTTP 409 on `generate`**. Latent for the whole project: `NoOpRecipePoolSource` kept plans empty (no slots, no day rows) and the single-kind ITs never hit it. **Fix:** group by `onDate` (the uniqueness key) + a `PlanPersisterTest` regression case.

### Un-pended (now green against the real pool/cold-start)
- **PLAN-18** mark a planned slot cooking; **PLAN-40** AI picks a candidate, plan carries scheduled recipes — both seed plannable recipes via the real `POST /api/v1/recipes`.
- **XJ-03** plan cooked + slot marked cooking from real scheduled recipes (cook leg; re-opt cascade stays out of scope).
- **XJ-06** cold start bootstraps the catalogue (empty catalogue + accept-all `DISCOVERY_FILTERING` stub → the `e2e` deterministic discovery source fills SYSTEM → `coldStart=true` + filled slots).
- Adds `TestPayloads.plannableRecipe` + a recipe-seeding step (12 recipes, 3×4 default slot kinds).

Still `@pending` (18): XJ-04 split (soft-pref merge unbuilt) + the other full-journeys / domain gaps tracked as backlog.

## Test plan
- [x] Local prod-parity stack: full suite `not @pending` → **125/125 green, 18 @pending**
- [x] `PlanPersisterTest` (regression) + spotless + `-Pe2e test-compile`
- [ ] CI: Build, test, lint (planner ITs + coverage) + E2E smoke

author: laurenbmoody-web
body:
…t-layout + features=keyValuePairs

ROOT CAUSE (from Supabase logs — raw Azure response):
  {"error":{"code":"NotFound","message":"Resource not found.",
   "innererror":{"code":"ModelNotFound",
    "message":"The requested model was not found."}}}

The function hit Azure's prebuilt-document model at api-version 2024-02-29-preview. That model was deprecated in 2023-10-31-preview and REMOVED in v4.0 (2024-11-30 GA). All PDF AND image uploads failed equally — not a media-type bug. The Layer 1/2/3 work from #27 was a real latent fix but covered a different failure mode.

Confirmed against Microsoft docs:
  • Migration path: prebuilt-layout with features=keyValuePairs.
    Microsoft explicitly: "With the addition of the keyValuePairs
    feature to prebuilt-layout, the layout model now produces the
    same results [as the deprecated prebuilt-document]."
  • Same $10/1000-pages pricing tier — no surprise cost. The
    features flag is NOT in the add-on pricing tier.
  • All four fields the parser consumes (analyzeResult.content,
    .tables, .paragraphs, .keyValuePairs) are present in
    prebuilt-layout responses (keyValuePairs gated on the features
    flag — see below).
  • DocumentKeyValuePair shape (kv.key.content, kv.value.content,
    confidence) is identical to the deprecated model's response —
    no parser body change needed.

Three surgical changes:

1. (header comment) Doc reference updated: "prebuilt-document model" → "prebuilt-layout model with features=keyValuePairs — replaces the deprecated prebuilt-document model that was removed in v4.0".

2. (line 36) AZURE_DOC_INTELLIGENCE_API_VERSION default bumped from '2024-02-29-preview' to '2024-11-30' (GA, stable). Env var override still wins when set.

3. (line 668) URL string: model name swapped AND features query parameter added. Multi-line inline comment above the URL site says EXPLICITLY: "⚠ DO NOT REMOVE the &features=keyValuePairs query parameter" — with rationale on what silently breaks if it's dropped (call still succeeds, line items still extracted from tables, but every metadata field silently nulls because keyValuePairs only comes back when the features flag is set). Silent metadata loss is much worse than loud failure — this is the documented landmine for a future edit and the comment makes the cost of removing the flag explicit.

NOT TOUCHED:
  • extractLineItems() — all four consumed fields present in new
    response; shape identical; no rewrite.
  • Polling logic, Claude name-expansion, modal, mediaType handling
    from #27 (all still correct, just orthogonal to this bug).

NOTE FOR LAUREN — env var override risk:
If AZURE_DOC_INTELLIGENCE_API_VERSION is set in Supabase function secrets to the old preview value, it WILL override the new default and reintroduce ModelNotFound. Either delete the secret (default kicks in) or update it to '2024-11-30'. Check Supabase dashboard before/after deploy.

Build: npm run build ✓.

## Summary
Refactored the `updatescoop.ps1` script to properly parse and manipulate the Scoop manifest as JSON instead of using string replacement. This makes the update process more robust and maintainable.

## Key Changes
- **Manifest parsing**: Changed from string replacement (`-replace` operations) to proper JSON parsing with `ConvertFrom-Json`
- **Direct property updates**: Now updates manifest properties directly (`$manifest.version`, `$manifest.architecture."64bit".url`, etc.) instead of replacing placeholder strings
- **JSON serialization**: Uses `ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10` to write the updated manifest back to disk
- **Updated zolam.json**: 
  - Version bumped to 1.0.3
  - URL updated to use actual version number
  - Hash updated with correct SHA256 value
  - Fixed bin entry to use proper array format: `[["zolam-windows-amd64.exe", "zolam"]]`
- **Documentation**: Added note to README clarifying that the winget package may lag behind releases due to PR requirements

## Implementation Details
The new approach is more maintainable because:
- JSON structure is preserved and validated during round-trip
- No risk of accidental string replacements in other parts of the manifest
- Easier to extend if manifest structure changes in the future
- Properly handles the nested architecture object structure

author: davidcozens
body:
## Purpose

Second story in epic **E28: lwIP Raw API support** (#439). Renames the
four FreeRTOS+TCP-specific networking adapter classes from
`SolidSyslogFreeRtos{Address,Datagram,Resolver,TcpStream}` to
`SolidSyslogPlusTcp*` and moves them from `Platform/FreeRtos/` to a new
`Platform/PlusTcp/` tree, so the forthcoming lwIP Raw backend
(S28.03–S28.05) can sit beside FreeRTOS-Plus-TCP without name
collisions. Pure cosmetic rename: no production behaviour change.

Closes #454.

## Change Description

**Class rename** (and file move from `Platform/FreeRtos/` to `Platform/PlusTcp/`):

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `SolidSyslogFreeRtosAddress` | `SolidSyslogPlusTcpAddress` |
| `SolidSyslogFreeRtosDatagram` | `SolidSyslogPlusTcpDatagram` |
| `SolidSyslogFreeRtosResolver` | `SolidSyslogPlusTcpResolver` |
| `SolidSyslogFreeRtosTcpStream` | `SolidSyslogPlusTcpTcpStream` |

The `TcpTcp` doubling is deliberate: `PlusTcp` is the backend
identifier, `TcpStream` is the abstraction name shared with
`SolidSyslogPosixTcpStream` / `SolidSyslogWinsockTcpStream` / the
forthcoming `SolidSyslogLwipRawTcpStream`. Same shape as the existing
sibling pattern.

`SolidSyslogFreeRtosMutex` and `SolidSyslogFreeRtosSysUpTime` **stay**
under `Platform/FreeRtos/` — RTOS primitives, not networking, reused
across both backends.

**Pool-size tunables renamed** in `Core/Interface/SolidSyslogTunablesDefaults.h`:
- `SOLIDSYSLOG_FREE_RTOS_DATAGRAM_POOL_SIZE` → `SOLIDSYSLOG_PLUS_TCP_DATAGRAM_POOL_SIZE`
- `SOLIDSYSLOG_FREE_RTOS_RESOLVER_POOL_SIZE` → `SOLIDSYSLOG_PLUS_TCP_RESOLVER_POOL_SIZE`
- `SOLIDSYSLOG_FREE_RTOS_TCP_STREAM_POOL_SIZE` → `SOLIDSYSLOG_PLUS_TCP_TCP_STREAM_POOL_SIZE`

`SOLIDSYSLOG_FREE_RTOS_MUTEX_POOL_SIZE` stays.

**CMake**. `Platform/PlusTcp/` is a new INTERFACE library `SolidSyslogPlusTcp`
mirroring `Platform/FreeRtos/`. The `SOLIDSYSLOG_FREERTOS_NET=BOTH`
path (S28.01 had it FATAL_ERROR) now emits a STATUS message and
compiles `PLUSTCP` only — silent synonym during the E28 gap, lifted in
S28.06. `LWIP` still FATAL_ERRORs.

**CI jobs** gain `-plustcp` suffix so the future lwIP siblings (S28.06)
can sit beside them:
- `build-freertos-host-tdd` → `build-freertos-host-tdd-plustcp`
- `build-freertos-target` → `build-freertos-target-plustcp`
- `bdd-freertos-qemu` → `bdd-freertos-qemu-plustcp`

Updated `needs:` arrays, JUnit artifact names, JUnit pattern strings in
the summary tool block, and the branch-protection list in `CLAUDE.md`.
Also added `Platform/PlusTcp/{Interface,Source}` to the cppcheck and
cppcheck-misra path lists in `ci.yml` (would have been silently dropped
from analysis otherwise).

**BDD common file renamed**: `BddTargetTlsSender_MbedTls_FreeRtosTcp.c`
→ `BddTargetTlsSender_MbedTls_PlusTcpTcp.c`.

**Pre-existing test wired in**: `SolidSyslogPlusTcpAddressTest`
(renamed from `SolidSyslogFreeRtosAddressTest`) was never in
`Tests/CMakeLists.txt:234`'s junit foreach list — built and passed on
its own but its JUnit XML was never emitted. Added in this PR rather
than deferred.

### Work shape

13 commits structured as 4 × (move-only) + 4 × (sed identifier rename),
then CI rename, docs sweep, format fallout fix, ci.yml cppcheck-path
fix, DEVLOG, and the Address-test junit fix. Move commits preserve 100%
git rename detection; rename commits drop below the 50% default
threshold on the smaller headers (15–30 lines, most lines touched by
sed) so `git log --follow` on the final names will track back through
the move but stop at the rename commit unless the reader passes
`--find-renames=10%`.

## Test Evidence

All pre-PR gates run locally green:

| Gate | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Format | `find Core/Interface Core/Source Tests Bdd/Targets Platform -name '*.c' -o -name '*.cpp' -o -name '*.h' \| xargs clang-format --dry-run --Werror` | clean |
| clang-tidy | `cmake --build --preset tidy` | exit 0 |
| cppcheck (style/warning/performance/portability) | `cmake --build --preset cppcheck` | exit 0 |
| cppcheck-misra | full Strict + Pragmatic source list with suppressions | exit 0 |
| IWYU | `cmake --build --preset iwyu --target iwyu` | no `should add` / `should remove` |
| FreeRTOS host-TDD | `cmake --build --preset debug --target junit` (in `cpputest-freertos`) | green, includes `SolidSyslogPlusTcpAddressTest` (11/11), `…DatagramTest` (30/30), `…ResolverTest` (20/20), `…TcpStreamTest` (49/49) |
| FreeRTOS cross-build | `cmake --build --preset freertos-cross --target SolidSyslogBddTarget` (in `cpputest-freertos-cross`) | links |
| CMake option variants | `cmake --preset freertos-cross -DSOLIDSYSLOG_FREERTOS_NET=PLUSTCP/LWIP/BOTH/BOGUS` | PLUSTCP builds; LWIP FATAL_ERRORs; BOTH STATUS+compiles PLUSTCP only; BOGUS validation error |

No new tests added — pure cosmetic rename. Existing test coverage runs
against the renamed classes; assertion bodies and target/file names
updated in lock-step with the source rename.

## Areas Affected

- **`Platform/PlusTcp/`** — new tree (Interface/, Source/, CMakeLists.txt).
- **`Platform/FreeRtos/`** — shrunk to Mutex + SysUpTime; CMakeLists.txt
  unchanged in shape, includes the same `Interface/` glob.
- **`Tests/FreeRtos/`** — four networking test targets renamed (sources
  re-pathed, target names updated, `.cpp` files renamed). The fifth
  pre-existing miss (Address test not in junit list) corrected in
  `Tests/CMakeLists.txt`.
- **`Bdd/Targets/FreeRtos/`** — `main.c` include lines + call sites,
  `CMakeLists.txt` source paths and include dirs, FreeRTOSIPConfig.h /
  mbedtls_user_config.h doc-comments.
- **`Bdd/Targets/Common/`** — `BddTargetTlsSender_MbedTls_FreeRtosTcp.c`
  renamed.
- **`Core/Interface/SolidSyslogTunablesDefaults.h`** — three pool-size
  tunable macros renamed.
- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** — three job key renames, dependent
  `needs:` arrays, JUnit artifact names, JUnit pattern strings, and the
  cppcheck / cppcheck-misra include path + source list additions.
- **Docs**: `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md` (branch-protection list + public-headers
  table), `docs/NAMING.md`, `docs/integrating-mbedtls.md`,
  `docs/misra-deviations.md`, `docs/iec62443.md`, `docs/rfc-compliance.md`,
  `docs/containers.md` (new "FreeRTOS networking backend selection"
  section), `Bdd/Targets/FreeRtos/README.md`.

## Breaking changes

- Public class headers `SolidSyslogFreeRtos{Address,Datagram,Resolver,TcpStream}.h`
  removed; replaced by `SolidSyslogPlusTcp*.h` siblings.
- Pool-size tunables `SOLIDSYSLOG_FREE_RTOS_{DATAGRAM,RESOLVER,TCP_STREAM}_POOL_SIZE`
  renamed to `SOLIDSYSLOG_PLUS_TCP_*` (impacts integrators overriding
  these in a user tunables header).
- CI job names changed — impacts anyone with branch-protection rules or
  external dashboards pinning the old names.
- BDD common file `BddTargetTlsSender_MbedTls_FreeRtosTcp.c` renamed to
  `BddTargetTlsSender_MbedTls_PlusTcpTcp.c`.

## Post-merge follow-ups for the maintainer

- **Live GitHub branch-protection settings**: update the required-status-check
  list to use `build-freertos-host-tdd-plustcp` / `build-freertos-target-plustcp`
  / `bdd-freertos-qemu-plustcp`. `CLAUDE.md`:28 documents the new names;
  GitHub's branch-protection panel needs the manual swap.

author: lockhart07
body:
## Why

Tournament data accumulates far too slowly to be meaningful under a day-window: Polymarket sees **~2.9 new unique markets/day**, and a candidate CID that's days old has single-digit resolved n. Day-gating (or a 7-day window) makes the tournament slice structurally near-empty; the meaningful frame is each active candidate's **all-time** record, growing daily.

This treats the tournament slice as the explicit carve-out to the rolling-window report restructure: **all-time only, scoped to candidates still under evaluation, never sample-gated.** Builds on #293 (already in main), which is what makes Polymarket tournament data exist at all.

## Changes (`analyze.py`)

- `load_active_tournament_cids()` — reads `tournament_tools.json` (the live candidate set); fails open to `None` (no scoping) on read error rather than hiding everything.
- `_scope_tournament_to_active()` — drops tournament-mode rows whose CID is no longer active; production rows untouched.
- `section_tournament_callouts(..., active_cids=)` — scopes to active CIDs and **drops the `CALLOUT_MIN_N` sample-size gate** so a candidate shows from its first resolved market; rows with `n < CALLOUT_MIN_N` carry a `⚠ low data` marker.
- `generate_report(..., active_tournament_cids=)` — scopes the all-time Tool×Version×Mode breakdown + callouts to active CIDs, and renders the **Last-Nd table production-only** (tournament never appears in a day-gated table). Removed the now-dead `rolling_scores_tournament` param and `--rolling-tournament` CLI plumbing.

## Changes (`notify_slack.py`)

Prompt surfaces every tournament callout and appends "(low data, still accumulating)" for `⚠ low data` rows instead of dropping them. (LLM-dependent; a deterministic append is a possible follow-up — the LLM has been observed to omit a lone low-n callout.)

## Verification (2026-05-25 run)

- **Polymarket** all-time tournament rows reduced to the 4 active CIDs; the high-n inactive tools (`prediction-online-sme` n=35, `prediction-url-cot` n=31) correctly hidden. Last-7d table: **0** tournament rows. Callout `superforcaster v0.20.0` (n=4) shown with `⚠ low data`.
- **Omen** active tournament slice is genuinely sparse right now (active `superforcaster` CID rotated in 05-23 → 0 resolved yet; active `factual_research` CID has only pre-#287 malformed markets resolved so far → `valid=0`, self-heals as post-#287 predictions resolve). Expected "grows daily" ramp, rendered correctly.
- Lint clean (`black-check`, `isort-check`, `flake8`, `mypy`, `pylint`, `darglint`); **303** tests pass, including new tests for active-CID scoping, the low-data marker (no longer suppressed), production-only Last-Nd table, and the loader.

author: gabiup2
body:
## Why this PR

External QA feedback (relayed via chat) flagged the v1.0.0 RC as "strong engineering, but publishing surface is under-verified — don't tag v1.0.0 from this state, you'll embarrass the good engineering." Every blocker turned out to be real on the current code. This PR fixes all four, plus three polish items, and verifies them by clean-venv install on this machine. **Open before merging PR #9 (dev → qa).**

## Blockers (verified fixed)

### 1. `uvx taskchampion-mcp` would fail — script alias missing
`pyproject.toml` only defined `taskchampion-mcp-server`; the README, four target install guides, and marketplace submission templates all tell users `uvx taskchampion-mcp`. uvx resolves by script name, not package name — so the marketplace's first action would have failed.

**Fix:** add `taskchampion-mcp = "taskchampion_mcp.server:main"` alongside the explicit binary. Both resolve to the same `main()`. Verified post-install: both `/tmp/check/bin/taskchampion-mcp --help` and `/tmp/check/bin/taskchampion-mcp-server --help` work.

### 2. Bundled schemas not in the wheel
`schemas/*.toml` lived at the repo root, was in the sdist include but **not** in the wheel (which packaged only `src/taskchampion_mcp/`). `default_schema_dir()` returned `<site-packages>/schemas/` (three levels up from `config.py`), which didn't exist on a real wheel install — the server would crash trying to load even the bundled minimal preset.

**Fix:** `git mv schemas src/taskchampion_mcp/schemas` so the directory lives inside the package and hatchling picks it up automatically. Update `default_schema_dir()` to return the in-package path. Drop the now-redundant `schemas/` from sdist's include list (the schemas still ship because they're under `src/`).

Verified: `unzip -l dist/*.whl | grep schemas | wc -l` returns 5 (one per preset, no duplicates). Clean-venv `list_available_schemas()` discovers all five.

### 3. Publish workflow had two real bugs
- `uv sync --dev` (wrong; needs `--extra dev` for our `[project.optional-dependencies]` layout)
- Missing the Taskwarrior/Timewarrior apt-install step that `ci.yml` has — tests would fail at first `task` shell-out

**Fix:** bring `publish.yml`'s test job in line with `ci.yml` (right `--extra dev` syntax, apt-install Taskwarrior+Timewarrior, bootstrap a non-interactive `.taskrc`). Also: skip `tests/targets` here (full target acceptance runs in `ci.yml`; the publish gate's job is "package works") and add a **built-artefact smoke step** that asserts `taskchampion_mcp/schemas/minimal.toml` is actually inside the wheel — catches the blocker-#2 regression class at build time.

### 4. mcp-publisher command syntax stale
Workflow used `mcp-publisher authenticate --github` but the current CLI is `mcp-publisher login github-oidc`. Updated, with a comment noting the registry CLI is still pre-1.0 and may shift again.

## Polish

5. **Marketplace tool-count corrected: 17 → 35**, with a curated headline list so reviewers see the shape (CRUD + lifecycle + time + reconfigure + introspection + onboarding) instead of a wall of names.
6. **Path fix in `docs/references/MCP_Registries.md`**: `.github/MARKETPLACE_SUBMISSIONS.md` → `docs/MARKETPLACE_SUBMISSIONS.md` (with a relative link).
7. **Stripped 21 files' `# Generated by: Claude / # Reviewed by: gabiup2` headers**. CONTRIBUTING.md already discloses AI-assisted contribution under the "LLM attribution" policy (lines 76, 138-153) — that's the right place. Per-file headers gave the "bulk-generated, owner-not-engaged" first impression the external reviewer flagged.

## Verification on this machine

- [x] `pytest tests/` → **444 passed, 26 skipped** (claude_desktop's manual scenarios)
- [x] `pytest --cov-fail-under=85` → **89.75 %** on `src/taskchampion_mcp/`
- [x] `ruff check src/ tests/` → **All checks passed**
- [x] `python tests/smoke_test_mcp.py` → both `onboarding` and `post_onboarding` scenarios green; 35 tools register in both modes
- [x] **Clean-venv install proof** (the QA feedback's mandatory test):
  ```
  rm -rf dist && uv build
  python3 -m venv /tmp/check && /tmp/check/bin/pip install dist/*.whl
  /tmp/check/bin/taskchampion-mcp --help       → works
  /tmp/check/bin/taskchampion-mcp-server --help → works
  ```
  `default_schema_dir()` returns `<site-packages>/taskchampion_mcp/schemas/` and all 5 presets are discoverable.

## What's still needed before tagging v1.0.0 (NOT in this PR)

The QA feedback's last recommendation: **don't tag `v1.0.0` from local code — tag `v1.0.0-rc1` first**. The publish workflow's smoke step now catches packaging regressions, but only a real PyPI install on a clean machine validates the wheel that PyPI actually serves.

Proposed final sequence after this PR + PR #9 merge:
1. Push `qa` → `main` (after the qa branch absorbs this PR via PR #9)
2. Tag `v1.0.0-rc1` from main → publish workflow uploads RC to PyPI
3. On a clean **Arch Linux laptop** (per server.json's `supported_platforms: ["linux", "macos"]`), run:
   ```bash
   uvx --from "taskchampion-mcp==1.0.0rc1" taskchampion-mcp --help
   uvx --from "taskchampion-mcp==1.0.0rc1" taskchampion-mcp --config-dump
   # Wire into claude code, run through the 26-scenario acceptance manually
   ```
4. **Only after RC passes**: tag `v1.0.0`, marketplace submissions follow.

## Reviewer judgement calls flagged in the PR body

- The `[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]` section now has no `force-include` because the directory lives inside the package. Confirm hatchling's auto-detection is the bar you want.
- mcp-publisher CLI command was updated against pre-1.0 registry docs; verify the syntax matches the version we'll be invoking when v1.0.0 tag lands.
- Stripping AI-attribution headers was operator-authorised verbally in chat ("Remove them"); CONTRIBUTING.md carries the central disclosure. If you'd rather keep them on a subset of files (e.g. the original onboarding work) say so and I'll restore selectively.

## Summary

Two operator-feedback fixes from 2026-05-28 (first organic Haiku firing on the public-topics soak):

Added `_scrub_preamble()` post-process belt-and-suspenders in `claude.generate_script` — drops everything before the canonical opener (fast path) or strips leading paragraphs matching known meta-narration patterns (fallback path). author: raghavchamadiya
body:
## Summary

Brings C and C++ ingestion up to JVM/Go/.NET parity for the workspace and include-graph layer:

- **CMake reader** (regex-tokenised) — `add_executable` / `add_library` / `target_sources` / `target_include_directories` / `target_compile_definitions` / `add_subdirectory` / `if(option)` conditional source tagging. Also parses `build/.cmake/api/v1/reply/` when present.
- **Bazel BUILD reader** — `cc_binary` / `cc_library` / `cc_test` / `cc_proto_library` / `cc_grpc_library` / `cc_fuzz_test`, with full label resolution (`//pkg:foo`, `:local`, plain filename).
- **`CppWorkspaceIndex`** unifying CMake + Bazel targets — `file_to_targets`, `public_header_includes` (literal + include-dir-stripped keys so `#include "leveldb/cache.h"` resolves without `compile_commands.json`), `project_export_macros` discovered from `#define X __declspec(dllexport)` patterns and `target_compile_definitions` ending in `*_EXPORT`/`*_API`. Built lazily under a new `graph.cpp_index` warmup phase.
- **Resolver rewrite** — six-step pipeline: `compile_commands` include dirs → workspace public-header map → per-target include-search-roots → importer-relative join → stdlib filter (silent drop) → stem fallback. New `resolve_cpp_import_all` fans header includes out to sibling TUs in shared targets, mirroring `resolve_java_import_all` / `resolve_go_import_all`.
- **Call resolver** — `_resolve_cpp_same_target` resolves bare identifier calls against any file sharing a CMake/Bazel target with the importer (confidence 0.85), mirroring the JVM/Go same-package strategies.
- **Project export macros** — the warmup re-tags `is_exported_symbol=True` on graph nodes whose signature text mentions a workspace-discovered macro (parser runs before warmup, so this is the cheapest propagation path).

### Validation (reindex of `test-repos/leveldb` + `test-repos/seastar`)

| Repo | unreachable_file | unused_export |
|---|---:|---:|
| **leveldb** baseline | 47 | 260 |
| **leveldb** after | **34** (−28%) | **159** (−39%) |
| **seastar** baseline | 64 | 206 |

seastar's `unreachable_file` is flat as expected — its `apps/**`, `demos/**`, `tests/perf/**`, `tests/fuzz/**` files surface via the multi-binary case which lands in the dead-code follow-up. The modest `unused_export` drop comes from project export macro discovery + same-target sibling edges.

No performance regression — leveldb 28.1s (vs 35s baseline), seastar 1m 17s (vs 1m 19s baseline).

author: lucvanrhyn
body:
## Summary

Closes #467. At ≤390px the dashboard KPI/stats strip clipped its rightmost **Active Alerts** chip off the right edge with no way to scroll to it (verified live via DOM measurement on prod).

**Root cause:** the strip (`components/dashboard/DashboardStatsStrip.tsx`) lives inside the single non-wrapping flex top bar in `components/dashboard/DashboardClient.tsx`, whose logotype / weather widget (`maxWidth: 380`) / controls siblings are all `flexShrink: 0`. The strip had `flex: 1` but no `minWidth: 0` and no overflow affordance, so its min-content width (chips are `whiteSpace: nowrap`) pinned it open and the overflow was **silently clipped** rather than scrollable.

**Fix (purely presentational — KPI values + data contract unchanged):**
- Strip container gets `minWidth: 0` → shrinks below its content width inside the flex row instead of pushing the `flexShrink:0` siblings off-screen.
- Strip container gets `overflowX: auto` → the overflow becomes an *intentional* horizontal scroll region rather than a silent clip.
- Each chip gets `flexShrink: 0` → labels stay readable instead of being crushed.

On desktop the chips fit, so no scrollbar shows and `justifyContent: center` still centers them — **the desktop top-bar layout is unchanged**. `DashboardClient.tsx` needed no change; the strip-only fix is the minimal, root-cause solution.

## Regression locks

- **`components/dashboard/__tests__/stats-strip-overflow.test.tsx`** (vitest, runs locally without a server) — pins the `minWidth:0` / `overflowX:auto` / per-chip `flexShrink:0` contract on both the single-species and multi-species (dual-chip) layouts. Drove the RED→GREEN cycle.
- **`e2e/dashboard-mobile-kpi.spec.ts`** (Playwright, live regression lock) — drives `/<slug>/dashboard` at 390px on **basson-boerdery** and **trio-b-boerdery**:
  - Active Alerts chip bounding-box right edge ≤ 390px (fully visible).
  - `document.documentElement.scrollWidth` ≤ 390px (no silent clip; the strip's own `overflow-x:auto` is an intentional nested scroll region that does not widen the document).
  - **Desktop guard at 1440px**: the strip is NOT scrolling (`scrollWidth ≈ clientWidth`), proving desktop layout is untouched.
  - Self-skips when `E2E_IDENTIFIER`/`E2E_PASSWORD` are unset (same pattern as `dashboard-counter-stability.spec.ts`).

## Test plan

- [x] vitest: new `stats-strip-overflow.test.tsx` 5/5 green; full `components/dashboard/` 6/6 green
- [x] `pnpm lint` — 0 errors
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — touched files clean (pre-existing baseline noise only, in unrelated test files)
- [x] `pnpm build` (`next build --webpack`, foreground) — EXIT 0, compiled successfully
- [ ] CI gate runs `e2e/dashboard-mobile-kpi.spec.ts` against the branch clone with seeded creds (see allow-list note below)

## Allow-list note (one item for human follow-up)

The new spec is gated by the explicit `testMatch` allowlist in `playwright.config.ts`, which is **outside this PR's file allow-list**, so the spec is not yet wired into the CI smoke run. It was verified to load, discover its 5 tests, and self-skip cleanly locally. To make it gate-blocking, add `'dashboard-mobile-kpi.spec.ts'` to `playwright.config.ts` `testMatch` (a one-line edit a maintainer can fold in, or I can do in a follow-up that includes that file in scope).

author: csviri
body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?
  
  This PR makes the dynamic-config ConfigMap **name** an explicit, configurable property and enforces it in the reconciler:

  1. Adds a new config option `spark.kubernetes.operator.dynamicConfig.name` (default: `spark-kubernetes-operator-dynamic-configuration`) in `SparkOperatorConf`.
  2. In `SparkOperatorConfigMapReconciler#reconcile`, short-circuits with `UpdateControl.noUpdate()` when the incoming ConfigMap's name does not match the configured value — so only the operator's intended ConfigMap can mutate
  `SparkOperatorConfManager` state and trigger a watched-namespace update.
  3. Documents the new property in `docs/config_properties.md`.
  4. Adds unit tests covering the new check (positive, negative, and custom-name path).

  ### Why are the changes needed?

  Previously the reconciler trusted any ConfigMap that matched the label selector configured via `spark.kubernetes.operator.dynamicConfig.selector` in the operator namespace. A user with `create configmap` permission in the
  operator namespace (but no broader operator privileges) could create a ConfigMap that matches the selector to:

  - Override `spark.kubernetes.operator.watchedNamespaces` and force the operator to start watching/reconciling namespaces it should not have access to.
  - More generally, override any dynamic-overridable operator property at runtime.

  Pinning the reconciler to a specific, configurable ConfigMap name closes this privilege-escalation path: a rogue ConfigMap with the right labels but a different name is now ignored.

  ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

  Yes (configuration). A new property is added:

  | Key | Default |
  | --- | --- |
  | `spark.kubernetes.operator.dynamicConfig.name` | `spark-kubernetes-operator-dynamic-configuration` |

  Operators that previously relied on a differently-named ConfigMap matching the dynamic-config selector must either rename their ConfigMap to the default value or set `spark.kubernetes.operator.dynamicConfig.name` to the
  existing name. The default matches the name used by the project's Helm chart, so standard deployments are unaffected.

  ### How was this patch tested?

  Added unit tests in `SparkOperatorConfigMapReconcilerTest`:

  - `reconcileSkipsConfigMapWithNonMatchingName` — a ConfigMap with a non-matching name is reconciled; verifies neither `namespaceUpdater` nor `watchedNamespacesGetter` are invoked and the rogue data does not leak into
  `SparkOperatorConfManager.configOverrides`.
  - `reconcileRefreshesConfigForMatchingName` — a ConfigMap with the configured name triggers the refresh path and the namespace-update callbacks; verifies the override is applied.
  - `reconcileHonorsCustomConfiguredConfigMapName` — when `dynamicConfig.name` is set to a custom value, the default-named ConfigMap is rejected and the custom-named one is processed.
  - The existing integration test (`sanityTest`, using `EnableKubeAPIServer`) was updated to use the matching ConfigMap name so it continues to exercise the end-to-end refresh path.

  ### Was this patch authored or co-authored using generative AI tooling?

A full visual polish and cleanup of the Reports area, plus a few behaviour fixes. Everything below in plain language.

## Report cards (grid view)
- The report name now comes first and bigger, in the app's normal font.
- Internal Audit and Bulk Audit now show as coloured pills (blue for Internal Audit, purple for Bulk Audit) so you can tell them apart at a glance. The pill sits next to the query count at the bottom.
- A soft purple glow follows your cursor over the cards, and the card border gently highlights when you hover.
- Download, share and delete buttons appear when you hover, all the same size, with a small text label when you point at each one.

## List view (made to match the grid view)
- Same report-name style, same coloured tags next to the query count, same hover buttons and labels.
- Added up/down sort arrows on the "Report" and "Generated" column headers so it's clear you can sort.

## Shared reports tab
- Now clearly shows reports that other people shared WITH you, instead of reading like reports you shared out to a team.
- Removed the old "Shared with [team]" label; the person who shared it is shown instead.

## Search and filters
- The search box background now matches the tag filter, so they look like one set of controls (in both grid and list).
- The "All Tags" filter menu was restyled to match the rest of the app's dropdowns.
- Clicking into any field in Reports now shows just a clean border (the extra purple glow ring was removed).

## Download / export preview
- Added a contents page after the cover page in the PowerPoint and Word previews.
- Moved the Download button into the modal's footer.
- Tidied the modal (removed an extra divider line and a label) and set a consistent width.

## Simpler severity
- Severity is now three levels only: High, Medium, Low. "Critical" was removed; those are now "High". Updated everywhere it appears (cards, tables, charts, legend).

## Cleanups and removals
- Made rounded corners, font sizes and icon sizes consistent across the whole Reports area.
- Standardised buttons (one main style, one secondary) and modal widths.
- Removed the "Generate Report" button (reports already come from a template).
- Removed the "Copy Workflow ID" button.
- Removed the extra "Data Source Files" tab from the comments panel (comments only now).
- Removed three unused report layouts, keeping the clean editorial one.
- Removed an unused status field from the query cards.

## Behaviour fixes
- Adding an observation now lets you upload multiple files at once.
- Switching a report to a different template now asks you to confirm first, so you don't lose content by accident.
- The template currently applied to a report is now clearly shown.

## New dependency
- Added the "gsap" animation library (powers the cursor glow on the cards).

## Test plan

- [ ] Open a report -> Download: check cover + contents page in PDF, PowerPoint and Word previews.

  - \`run\` / \`run_shell\` — dry-run 인지 + 로깅 일원화
- \`devenv/cli/_platform.py\` — \`ensure_linux()\` 가드 (macOS / WSL 차단)
- \`devenv/cli/_{dir,zsh,vim,tmux}.py\` — 기존 Bash 스크립트 4개의 동작을 1:1 재현. 외부 인스톨러(oh-my-zsh)는 \`run_shell\`로, 그 외는 모두 헬퍼 조합

### B. dotfile 자산 이동 (\`packages/\` → \`devenv/packages/\`)

- \`pyproject.toml\`의 \`[tool.setuptools.package-data]\`에 등록 → wheel install 시 함께 배포
- 접근은 \`importlib.resources\` 기반 \`package_file(\"zsh\", \"zshrc\")\` 헬퍼만 사용 (경로 하드코딩 금지)

### C. Bash 인프라 정리

- \`scripts/install_{dir,zsh,vim,tmux}.sh\` 4개 **삭제** (CLI에서 흡수)
- \`scripts/install_packages.sh\` 신설 — \`uv sync\` + \`uv pip install -e .\` + \`pre-commit install\` 부트스트랩
- \`Makefile\` 슬림화 — \`install / lint / test / clean / help\`만 남기고 모두 uv에 위임. \`make install\` = **개발자 부트스트랩**, \`devenv install\` = **실제 환경 설치**로 의미 분리

### D. Python 패키징 / 품질 도구

- \`pyproject.toml\` — \`linux-devenv\` 패키지, \`devenv = \"devenv.cli:cli\"\` 엔트리, click 8.x 의존
- ruff + ty + pytest + pre-commit 설정 (\`devenv/packages/\`는 ruff exclude — zsh/vim 문법이라 Python lint 부적합)
- \`.pre-commit-config.yaml\` — ruff / ty / bashate / markdownlint. bashate는 \`devenv/packages/\` 사용자 dotfile 제외, markdownlint는 \`.github/\` PR 템플릿 제외

### E. 테스트 추가 (\`tests/unit_test/\`)

- \`conftest.py\` — \`fake_home\` / \`ctx\` / \`dry_ctx\` fixture로 실제 \`\$HOME\` 격리
- \`test_installer.py\` — 헬퍼 단위 (멱등성, 백업, dry-run 비파괴, 명령 누락 감지)
- \`test_cli.py\` — \`CliRunner\` 기반 CLI 스모크 (help / version / where / setup / list / install --dry-run / 옵션 충돌)

### F. Claude Code 에이전트 가이드

- \`CLAUDE.md\` — 페르소나, rule index, Claude 한정 운영 원칙 8개(Plan-First / idempotency / Linux-only / no destructive defaults / no secrets / cli vs packages 분리 / uv only / 한국어 응답)
- \`.claude/rules/project-context.md\` — 디렉토리 구조, \`devenv/cli/\` ↔ \`devenv/packages/\` 역할 분리, 새 도구 추가 시나리오
- \`.claude/rules/build-and-test.md\` — uv 사용 규칙, devenv CLI 표면, 컨테이너 스모크, 멱등성 검증
- \`.claude/rules/coding-conventions.md\` — Python 스타일(Ruff 119자, Google docstring, ty), Click 컨벤션(exit code 0/1/2, \`--help\` 한국어 / docstring 영어), idempotency 패턴, dotfile 규칙
- \`.claude/rules/contribution-guide.md\` — 브랜치 / 커밋 / PR 컨벤션, 리뷰 기준, 체크리스트

### G. 문서 정비

- \`README.md\` — skills 레포 스타일로 재작성 (이전 311줄 → 141줄). 사용자 사용법은 \`devenv <cmd> --help\`로 위임
- \`CONTRIBUTING.md\` — 신규. installer 작성 패턴 + 체크리스트 3종(CLI 로직 / dotfile / Python 의존)

### H. GitHub Actions 조정 (self-hosted → ubuntu-latest)

- 9개 워크플로우 전부 \`runs-on: ubuntu-latest\`
- \`fetch-secrets\` 잡 + Harbor 사설 컨테이너 + 사설 PyPI publish 모두 제거 (\`pre-commit\`, \`pytest-helper\`, \`release-package\`, \`uv-lock-update\`)
- uv 설치는 \`astral-sh/setup-uv@v5\`로 일원화
- \`unit-test.yml\`의 \`paths\` 트리거: \`skills/**\` → \`devenv/**\` 교정
- \`release-package.yml\`: PyPI publish 단계 제거, GitHub Release(.whl 첨부)만 유지
- pytest 커버리지 기본 \`true\` → \`false\` (\`pytest-cov\` 미포함)

## 5. 테스트 계획 (Test Plan)

로컬 검증 완료:

- \`uv run --no-sync pytest tests/unit_test\` → **17 / 17 PASSED**
- \`uv run --no-sync pre-commit run --all-files\` → 모든 훅 통과 (ruff-format, ruff, ty, trailing-whitespace, end-of-file-fixer, check-yaml, bashate, markdownlint)
- \`uv run --no-sync devenv --help\` → 모든 subcommand 노출 확인
- \`uv run --no-sync devenv doctor\` → 선행 명령 5개 + Linux 가드 통과
- \`uv run --no-sync devenv install --only dir --dry-run --home /tmp/_dh\` → dry-run 시 \`/tmp/_dh\`는 그대로, 실행될 명령만 출력
- \`uv run --no-sync devenv list --home /tmp/_dh\` → 모든 도구 \`[missing]\` 정상 표시

CI에서 추가로 검증되는 부분:

- ubuntu-latest 기반 \`pre-commit-validation\` 워크플로우
- \`unit-test\` 워크플로우(\`pytest-helper.yml\`)
- \`pr-title-checker\` / \`pr-size-labeler\`

추가 권장 검증(머지 전):

- 깨끗한 Ubuntu 22.04 컨테이너에서 \`uv pip install -e . && devenv install --yes\` 끝까지 실행
- 동일 컨테이너에서 \`devenv install\` 두 번 연속 → 두 번째도 깨지지 않음 (멱등성)

## 6. 리뷰어에게 (To Reviewers)

리뷰어에게 특별히 강조하고 싶거나 확인을 요청하고 싶은 부분이 있다면 작성해주세요.

- [x] 제 코드가 프로젝트의 코드 스타일 가이드라인을 따릅니다.
- [x] 제 코드가 새로운 경고를 발생시키지 않습니다.
- [x] 변경 사항에 대한 테스트를 작성했습니다.
- [x] 기존 테스트가 모두 통과합니다.
- [x] 필요한 경우 문서(documentation)를 업데이트했습니다.

### 중점 리뷰 포인트

1. **멱등성 / 비파괴 동작** — \`deploy_dotfile\`이 timestamp 백업을 기본으로 하고 \`--force\`만 생략하는 정책이 적절한지
2. **CLI 옵션 표면** — \`--only\` / \`--skip\` / \`--force\` / \`--dry-run\` / \`--yes\` / \`--home\` 조합이 직관적인지, 이름 변경 의견
3. **Claude Code 룰 분배** — \`CLAUDE.md\` ↔ 4개 \`.claude/rules/\` 토픽 분할이 균형 잡혔는지, 누락 토픽 여부
4. **CI 단순화** — Harbor / 사설 PyPI / fetch-secrets 제거로 잃은 기능 중 다시 살려야 할 것이 있는지 (특히 \`release-package.yml\`의 사설 PyPI publish)
5. **브랜치 이름 vs 스코프** — 브랜치명은 \`HOTFIX\`이지만 실제 변경은 Feature 스케일. 커밋 메시지 태그는 \`[Feature]\`, PR 제목은 스킬 규칙대로 \`[HOTFIX]\`로 작성. PR 제목 변경 의견 환영

author: aswinmcw
body:
### Goal
Drive the sweep-validation pass rate to **100% on both the lead-model and non-lead-model `model_traced` suites**. The validation surfaced a long tail of failures — ~33 `mesh_device_shape` mismatches (Galaxy configs traced on one mesh, e.g. 4x8, running on another, e.g. 8x4), plus wrong dispatch axis, cross-vector device-cache contamination, blackhole/p100a/p300a misrouting, and op-specific reconstruction/golden bugs — that this PR fixes so every traced config runs on the right hardware/mesh and validates correctly.

### What is changed
Mesh-shape filtering is implemented via a `MESH_DEVICE_SHAPE` environment-variable filter in `framework/vector_source.py`, driven by `framework/compute_validation_sweep_matrix.py` now emitting a non-empty `mesh_device_shape` for single-mesh groups. (Note: `matrix_runner_config.py`'s `hw` policy still uses `enforce_mesh_capability=False`; mesh filtering is done by the env filter, not that flag.)

Alongside it, the broader set of fixes needed to reach 100% on both lead and non-lead model suites:
- **Hardware routing** — correct p100a/p150b/p300a/blackhole lane selection and dispatch-core handling (`create_mesh_device`, CI workflow routing).
- **Dispatch axis** — per-vector WORKER ROW/COL selection derived from each op's traced `program_config` grid (`mesh_tensor_utils.py`).
- **Device-cache hygiene** — per-vector device-cache disable for model-traced runs and CCL sub-device-manager cleanup to stop cross-vector state leakage (`ccl_common.py`, `all_gather_async`).
- **Op-specific reconstruction/golden fixes** — e.g. paged-SDPA decode (`sub_core_grids` reconstruction, padded-head Q layout, valid paged page_table generation), plus per-op golden/placement fixes across the `model_traced` sweeps.

### Notes for reviewers
- Scope is ~57 files (CI workflows, runner routing, per-vector device cache, dispatch logic, and many op-specific golden/reconstruction fixes) — not a one-line change. The earlier "one-line change in matrix_runner_config.py" note was inaccurate (thanks @Copilot) and has been corrected here.
- When `MESH_DEVICE_SHAPE` is set (from mesh-split batches), vectors with non-matching traced mesh shapes are filtered out; when it is unset (non-split batches), filtering falls back to `allowed_mesh_shapes` from the test-group capability.

author: afadil
body:
## Problem

When an account is created, updated, or deleted — including toggling **Hide** (`isActive`) or **Archive** (`isArchived`, which removes the account from the portfolio) — the frontend only invalidated \`ACCOUNTS\` and the spending caches. Holdings, portfolio summary, performance, valuation, and net-worth caches stayed stale in the UI until the backend's async portfolio recalc finished and emitted \`portfolio:update-complete\`.

## Fix

Reuse the same \`shouldInvalidateAfterPortfolioUpdate\` predicate the portfolio-update event handler already uses, extracted into a shared module (\`apps/frontend/src/lib/query-invalidation.ts\`) so both call sites share a single source of truth.

The predicate invalidates everything **except** cloud/broker/subscription/sync queries (which have their own lifecycle), so it covers holdings, portfolio totals, performance, valuation, net worth, accounts, spending — without unnecessarily refetching broker connections, subscription plans, user info, etc.

This also makes the previous explicit \`SPENDING_SETTINGS\` + \`invalidateSpendingCaches\` calls redundant (the predicate covers them), so they were removed along with their now-unused imports.

## Changes

- **New** \`apps/frontend/src/lib/query-invalidation.ts\` — shared predicate + cloud-sync exclusion set.
- \`apps/frontend/src/use-global-event-listener.ts\` — imports the predicate from the shared module instead of defining it locally.
- \`apps/frontend/src/pages/settings/accounts/components/use-account-mutations.ts\` — \`invalidateAccountDependentQueries\` collapsed to a single predicate-driven invalidation.

## Verification

- \`pnpm type-check\` ✅
- \`pnpm lint\` — 0 errors (pre-existing warnings unrelated to changed files)

author: diogenesmendes01
body:
Closes #255

**STACKED ON #243** — base branch is `claude/issue-234-ksm-tenant-agent-guard` (NOT `main`). The fix builds on the per-row `runWithTenantContext` structure that PR #243 introduced. If #243 merges first, GitHub will auto-retarget this to `main` and the diff stays clean.

## Summary

PR #243 (issue #234) added per-row `runWithTenantContext` so the rule mutations in `KnowledgeStateMachine.transition` are correctly scoped to (tenant_id, agent_id). But the `cognitive_module_log` audit row — written by `runner.ts:59-73` via `tryGetCurrentContext()` — was driven by the OUTER `runCognitiveModule('knowledge-state-machine.auto-promoter', ...)` wrap that enclosed the whole worker body. That outer wrap ran BEFORE the per-row context was established, so the audit row landed on `('default','default')`. A single batch tick spanning N tenants collapsed all execution attribution into the `default` bucket — a metadata leak (audit/metrics, not data) across tenants.

Codex re-validation of PR #243 surfaced this. This PR fixes it by:

1. Moving the `runCognitiveModule` wrap INSIDE the per-row `runWithTenantContext` block so `tryGetCurrentContext()` reads the row's persisted tenant_id+agent_id when it writes the audit row.
2. Removing the outer `runCognitiveModule` wrap — its attribution was the leak.
3. Preserving the batch-level summary as a plain `logger.info` line so operators still see a single 'tick.done' marker per cron tick.

## Choice — per-row N audits vs. single outer audit with explicit tenant

**Per-row** (chosen). A single batch can span multiple tenants (`listEligible` returns rows from any tenant whose lifecycle_status matches the SQL filter), so the outer-batch wrap has NO single valid tenant to attribute to. The alternative — keeping the outer wrap and passing an explicit `tenant_id` to the audit-write — would still mis-attribute every tenant other than the one we pick. Per-row is the only semantically correct option for a multi-tenant batch.

**Trade-off**: the cron tick now emits N audit records instead of 1. At the per-tick worst case (`PER_TICK_LIMIT=100 × 4 KINDS × 6 promote stages = 2400` max records/tick, in practice far less because rows don't all transition through every stage), with the worker running hourly, this is bounded and well within `cognitive_module_log` capacity. Index `cognitive_module_log_tenant_agent_idx` (on tenant_id, agent_id, created_at) makes per-tenant queries efficient even at higher record counts. The batch-level summary log line (`knowledge_state_promoter.tick.done`) is preserved so the operator-visible 'tick did N things' marker is unchanged.

## Test counts

- New: `tests/unit/workers/knowledge-state-promoter-audit-tenant.spec.ts` — **4 tests** (multi-tenant attribution, empty eligible set, per-row context propagates to BOTH mutation AND audit, status preserved across row loop).
- Verification (all green):
  - `npx vitest run tests/unit/workers/` — 4/4 pass.
  - `npx vitest run tests/unit/control-plane/knowledge-state-machine/` — #243's ksm-rules-cross-tenant.spec.ts (23 tests) still green.
  - `npx vitest run tests/integration/p10a-knowledge-lifecycle.spec.ts` — 8/8 pass.
  - `npx vitest run tests/property/knowledge-state-machine.spec.ts` — 6/6 pass.
  - `npx vitest run tests/unit/cognition-runner.spec.ts tests/unit/audit-tenant-fallback.spec.ts` — 10/10 pass.
  - `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean.
  - `npx eslint <touched files>` — clean.

- `src/workers/knowledge-state-promoter.ts` (256 insertions, 103 deletions — most of the diff is comment expansion + reorganization)
- `tests/unit/workers/knowledge-state-promoter-audit-tenant.spec.ts` (NEW)

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
This PR cleans up abandoned ephemeral Redis consumer groups without inferring consumer liveness from Redis stream idle metadata.

Previously, only groups with zero consumers were cleaned up. Ungraceful shutdowns (SIGKILL, OOM-kill, pod eviction) can still leave ephemeral groups with consumer entries behind, and those groups can block stream trimming or accumulate over time.

The safer cleanup model is explicit liveness: new ephemeral subscriptions use heartbeat-managed group names and refresh a Redis heartbeat key while the subscription context is alive. Cleanup and trimming treat those groups as stale only after the heartbeat expires. Legacy `ephemeral-*` groups with consumers are preserved because they cannot be safely distinguished from live subscribers during rollout.

<details>
<summary>Changes</summary>

**`prefect_redis/messaging.py`**
- Generates heartbeat-managed ephemeral group names for new ephemeral subscriptions
- Maintains a Redis heartbeat key with a TTL based on `trim_idle_threshold`
- Uses heartbeat expiry, not `XINFO CONSUMERS` `idle`, to skip and delete stale heartbeat-managed groups
- Keeps the original zero-consumer ephemeral group cleanup behavior
- Removes Redis server-version probing and the cleanup dependency on `INFO`

**`tests/test_messaging.py`**
- Covers heartbeat key lifecycle for ephemeral subscriptions
- Covers cleanup of expired heartbeat-managed groups and preservation of live or legacy groups
- Covers trimming behavior for stale vs. live heartbeat-managed groups
</details>

author: jay20012024
body:
## Summary

Two real regressions from `reference/export_example.pdf` that no agent pass caught:

1. **Wide tables clipped** — article had `max-width: 38em` even in print, so any block element wider than ~530px silently cropped. A 10-column comparison table lost its right 3 columns.
2. **Empty page 1** — `table { break-inside: avoid }` pushed the whole table to a fresh page, leaving the previous page half-blank.

## Fix

- Article `max-width: none` in print; reading measure (38em) re-applied to paragraph-level elements only — `:is(p, ul, ol, blockquote, h1-h6)`
- Tables: `break-inside: auto` (was `avoid`); `tr` gets the `break-inside: avoid` instead so rows don't split mid-row
- `thead { display: table-header-group }` for per-page header repeat (browser support varies)
- Print-specific table density: `0.85em` font, tight padding, word-wrap on cells

## Meta-lesson

Three rounds of agent review (naive client / FE senior / UI/UX worker) shipped a clean review every time on these print rules — none could open an actual print preview. The verifier needs a real browser (Playwright / headless Chrome) for print-flow regressions. Filing as follow-up.

body:
## Summary
- Move pure OSPF redistribution route transformation into `internal/domain/routing/ospf`.
- Split external metric and route type helpers out of SPF code.
- Keep controlplane orchestration focused on candidate collection, VRF filtering, and route-policy application.

## Background / Why
Issue #93 calls out that `engine/controlplane` was mixing OSPF-specific external route mutation with orchestration. The reusable protocol transformation now lives in the OSPF domain package.

## What Changed
- Added `RedistributedExternalRoute` to rewrite a candidate RIB entry into an OSPF external route with AD 110, metric type, route type, and metric selection.
- Kept `ospfRedistributionCandidates` and route-map evaluation in `engine/controlplane`.
- Added domain tests for OSPF attribute rewriting and metric precedence: explicit redistribution metric, BGP MED, source metric, then default 20.

## Behavior / Impact
No intended convergence or route semantic change. For example, when `r1` redistributes a BGP route like `203.0.113.0/24` into OSPF, the resulting E1/E2 route attributes are produced by the OSPF domain helper while the engine still decides when redistribution runs and which candidates are eligible.

## Verification
- `go test ./internal/domain/routing/ospf ./internal/engine/controlplane` passed.
- `go test ./...` passed.

## Risk and Rollback
Low risk; this is a scoped refactor covered by existing controlplane tests plus new domain tests. Roll back by reverting this PR.

## Notes for Reviewers
Please check the boundary between `engine/controlplane` orchestration and `domain/routing/ospf` transformation logic.

Closes #93

body:
## Summary

Goes-live readiness for harvesting AtmosFlow AI (Jasper) Q+A pairs into a future fine-tuning corpus. Strictly scoped per the approved plan. Engine code is untouched; persistence behavior is unchanged — chats are still saved on every turn, and consent only filters the export pipeline.

Three things were missing before today's data was fine-tuning-grade; this PR adds all three:

1. **Legal basis** — opt-out consent flag on `profiles`, default-on, with a new "AI improvement program" section on the privacy policy + a 30-day notice email renderer for existing users.
2. **Quality signal** — Lucide thumbs-up / thumbs-down icons under every settled assistant turn (no emoji glyphs); thumbs-down expands an optional "what was wrong?" reason input. Backed by a new `field_assistant_feedback` table with owner-only RLS.
3. **Per-turn telemetry on the message row** — model, input/output tokens, tool rounds, latency. Avoids an audit-log join at export time.

Plus a JSONL exporter (`scripts/export-finetune-dataset.mjs`) that skips opt-out users + excludes 👎 turns by default, with `--include-negatives` for DPO/preference-pair use later.

## What's in here

**Schema** — `supabase/migrations/015_ai_training_consent.sql`
- `profiles.ai_training_consent` (NOT NULL DEFAULT true) + `ai_training_consent_updated_at` + `training_notice_sent_at`
- New columns on `field_assistant_messages`: `model`, `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `tool_rounds`, `latency_ms` (all nullable so historical rows don't need backfill)
- New table `field_assistant_feedback` with UNIQUE(message_id) so UPSERT is idempotent; owner-only RLS + `set_updated_at` trigger with pinned `search_path`

**API**
- `api/field-assistant.ts` — pre-generates `assistantTurnId`, emits it as `assistant_message_id` on the SSE meta event, measures latency around `runAgentLoop`, persists telemetry on the assistant row
- `api/field-assistant-feedback.ts` (new) — `POST { message_id, rating, reason? }` → UPSERT, filtered by `user_id` with an assistant-turn-only guard
- `api/field-assistant-history.ts` — LEFT-JOINs feedback on `get` so resumed conversations show existing ratings

**Hook + UI**
- `useFieldAssistant.submitFeedback(dbId, rating, reason?)` — optimistic local flip + rollback on failure; threads `assistant_message_id` from meta onto the streaming bubble's `dbId`
- `src/components/ui/JasperFeedbackRow.jsx` (new) — Lucide `ThumbsUp` / `ThumbsDown` icons, thumbs-down expands a one-line reason input + Submit / Skip
- `src/components/Icons.jsx` — registers `thumbsUp` / `thumbsDown` via the Lucide map

**Consent + legal**
- `components/account/AccountSettings.tsx` — new "AI improvement program" section with default-on toggle + opt-out copy
- `src/components/LegalScreens.jsx` (privacy policy) — new section 5 "AI Improvement Program" with what's collected, what's scrubbed, opt-out path, 30-day effective date; downstream sections renumbered
- `lib/email/training-program-notice.ts` (new) — 30-day notice email renderer (cron wiring intentionally not auto-sent yet)
- `lib/ai-training-consent.ts` (new) — `userConsentsToTraining` + batch `filterConsentingUserIds`; fail-closed on errors

**Export pipeline**
- `scripts/export-finetune-dataset.mjs` (new) — JSONL exporter with `--since`, `--out`, `--dry-run`, `--include-negatives`, `--system-prompt`; pure `buildTrainingRows` exported separately for testing

**Tests + acceptance**
- `tests/api/field-assistant-feedback.test.ts` — 10 tests pinning the auth, validation, UPSERT, and re-rating contract
- `tests/scripts/export-finetune-dataset.test.ts` — 5 tests pinning consent-filtering, thumbs-down exclusion, conversation pairing, telemetry propagation
- `tests/components/jasper-feedback-row.test.tsx` — 6 tests pinning the UI contract
- 3 new acceptance criteria: `AI-TRAINING-CONSENT`, `FEEDBACK-WRITE-PATH`, `EXPORT-PIPELINE`

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run lint` — clean
- [x] `npm run typecheck` — clean
- [x] `npm run test` — 1698/1703 pass (5 pre-existing skips)
- [x] `npm run build` — clean
- [x] `npm run accept:prod-ready` — **42/42**
- [ ] Apply `supabase/migrations/015_ai_training_consent.sql` to the live Supabase project (deferred — needs your MCP approval at deploy time)
- [ ] Manual smoke: open AtmosFlow AI → ask a question → confirm thumbs-up/thumbs-down row renders after the stream settles → tap thumbs-down → type a reason → confirm a row lands in `field_assistant_feedback`
- [ ] Manual: Settings → AI improvement program → flip off → send a new question → confirm the message row still persists but `ai_training_consent = false`
- [ ] `node scripts/export-finetune-dataset.mjs --since 2026-01-01 --dry-run` after migration — confirm the row count excludes opted-out users and 👎 turns

## Out of scope (per the plan)

- The fine-tuning run itself (separate workstream — driven by a notebook + the exported JSONL)
- A "regenerate" affordance on the chat (different signal model — defer)
- Preference-pair / DPO labeling UI (`--include-negatives` is enough until we have volume)
- Per-finding accuracy labels from the assessor (separate workstream needing a labeling sheet)
- Cron / admin wiring to actually send the 30-day notice email (renderer is in; sender + `training_notice_sent_at` stamping is a follow-up)

body:
# [PR] 적(Enemy) 시스템 지형 인식 및 AI 고도화

## 🎯 주요 목표
새롭게 적용된 지형 시스템(`LevelLayout`)을 적들이 완벽히 인식하게 하고, 벽을 통과하거나 막히는 문제를 해결하여 보다 지능적인 전투 환경을 조성함.

---

## 🚀 주요 변경 사항

### 1. 지형 충돌(Collision) 완벽 지원
*   **문제**: 적들이 벽을 인식하지 못하고 뚫고 지나가는 현상 발생.
*   **해결**: `CollisionSystem`의 충돌 대상을 "Player"에서 "Enemy" 포함 전체 유동 객체로 확장하여 벽과의 물리적 상호작용을 구현함.

### 2. 지능적 장애물 우회 AI 구현
*   **문제**: 적들이 벽에 막혔을 때 플레이어를 쳐다만 보고 멈춰 있는 현상 발생.
*   **해결**: **Simple Steering AI**를 도입. 이동 경로에 벽이 감지되면 좌우(45도, 90도) 경로를 탐색하여 우회로를 찾도록 개선함.

### 3. 안전한 스폰(Spawn) 위치 검증
*   **문제**: 적이 벽 내부나 장애물 위에서 생성되어 끼이는 현상 발생.
*   **해결**: `IsPositionBlocked` 유틸리티를 활용, 안전한 위치(벽이 아닌 곳)가 확인될 때까지 위치 탐색 후 생성하도록 로직 보완.

### 4. 코드 안정성 및 버그 수정
*   **Access Violation 해결**: `EnemySpawner`와 `EnemyController` 간의 참조 권한을 정리하여 런타임 크래시 방지.
*   **문서화**: 커밋 이력 및 상세 변경 사항을 `AI_UPDATE_LOG.md`에 별도로 기록함.

---

## 🧪 테스트 결과
*   [x] 적이 벽을 뚫고 지나가지 않음.
*   [x] 적이 벽 뒤에 있는 플레이어를 향해 옆으로 돌아서 접근함.
*   [x] 적이 벽 안에서 소환되지 않음.
*   [x] 30마리 이상 스폰 시 프레임 드랍 및 크래시 없음.

---

Github has a single event for triggering on[ issue_comment](https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads#issue_comment). Instead of filtering for only PRs, which we need for the CLA automation we want to build, I am just passing that through completely. Our github app already has permission to track these.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches webhook ingress and trigger matching for a new event shape; production apps must subscribe to `issue_comment` on GitHub, and comment volume could increase agent runs if broadly enabled.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **`issue_comment.created`** as a selectable GitHub trigger so agents can run on new comments on **issues and pull requests** (not PR-only).
> 
> The **Probot app** subscribes to `issue_comment`, handles `issue_comment.created`, and forwards issue/comment metadata plus an **`isPullRequest`** flag via the unified GitHub event API. **Types and ingress parsing** introduce `issue` + `comment` on `GithubTrigger`, extend the SDK with `GithubIssueCommentCreatedTrigger`, and update presenters/run-history metadata. The **backend integration** matches triggers by `eventType`, uses comment-scoped **entity IDs**, skips PR file attachment fetching for comment events, and can **sample** recent repo comments when that event type is configured.

body:
Fixes #2142

> **Stacked on #2141.** The ACL-dependency infrastructure (the `dependsOn`
> field, `resolveAclDependencyDiagnostics`, the spec) lives only on
> `feat/acl-dependency-bundles` and is not yet on `develop`, so this PR is
> based on that branch. **Merge #2141 first**, then retarget this PR's base
> to `develop` (the diff will reduce to just the sales changes).

## Problem
PR #2141 shipped the ACL dependency-bundles infrastructure and used
`customers` as the reference module. Every other module still needs its
`acl.ts` updated. Sales is the headline case from @alinadivante's QA finding
on PR #2073: granting `sales.orders.view` without channel/settings access
produces a 403 toast-storm on the Orders page, because the order/quote pages
(guarded by `sales.orders.view`) fetch channel/settings/methods GET endpoints
that today require `.manage`.

## What Changed
- **New split features** in `sales/acl.ts`: `sales.channels.view` and
  `sales.settings.view` — read access carved out of the corresponding
  `.manage` features so dependent pages can ask for read access without
  escalating to manage.
- **`dependsOn` declared on every sales feature** per spec §6.2. Verified
  every cross-module dependency id exists on `develop`
  (`customers.people.view`, `catalog.products.view`, `currencies.view`,
  `shipping_carriers.view`, `payment_gateways.view`).
- **Refinement of §6.2**: `sales.documents.number.edit` depends on
  `sales.orders.view` only — dropped the spec's spurious `configs.manage`.
  That feature gates per-document inline number editing on the order/document
  detail page (`documents/[id]/page.tsx`, `documents/factory.ts`); it has no
  relationship to the `configs` module admin capability, so depending on it
  would generate a false "missing dependency" warning.
- **`setup.ts`**: granted `sales.channels.view` + `sales.settings.view` to the
  `employee` role (admin keeps the `sales.*` wildcard, which already covers
  them).

## Tests
New `packages/core/src/modules/sales/__tests__/acl-dependencies.test.ts` (5 cases):
- the two split view features exist;
- **no `unknownReferences`** for any sales feature against the combined
  catalog (sales + every referenced sibling module) — the issue's acceptance
  criterion;
- granting `sales.orders.view` alone surfaces the expected missing
  dependencies (`sales.channels.view`, `sales.settings.view`,
  `customers.people.view`, `catalog.products.view`, `currencies.view`) — the
  #2073 toast-storm scenario, now warned about at edit time;
- `.manage` features depend on their split `.view` feature;
- default role features cover the new view features.

Validation: new suite 5/5; `@open-mercato/shared` resolver 19/19 and
`@open-mercato/core` auth features API 6/6 still green; core `tsc --noEmit`
clean; `build:packages` 19/19; `yarn generate` no tracked drift.

## Backward Compatibility
Additive only — two new ACL feature ids and optional `dependsOn` metadata; no
feature id removed or renamed; exported `features` shape preserved; no API,
event, DI, import-path, or DB changes. Per spec §4.6 this is warnings-only;
no save is blocked.

## Follow-up (out of scope)
This PR is the **declarative** deliverable from the issue (new view features +
`dependsOn` + default-role grants + tests). It does **not** yet relax the
order/quote-page read endpoints (`/api/sales/channels`, `/shipping-methods`,
`/payment-methods`, `/settings/*`, `/tax-rates`, `/adjustment-kinds`,
`/price-kinds`) from `.manage` to the new `.view` features. That endpoint
re-wire is what actually stops the 403 toast-storm at runtime; it's an RBAC
contract change with BC nuance (`requireFeatures` is all-of and `.manage`
does not imply `.view`, so custom roles holding only `.manage` would need a
`.view` grant) and is best handled as its own change. Recommend a follow-up
issue to relax those GET guards once this lands.

## 背景

D2 中庸路径 **Phase 2**。Stack 在 #179(Phase 1 公共类型 + adapter)之上,落地 `ExtensionRegistry` skeleton。

## Phase 2 范围(本 PR)

**仍是零接入,零生产影响。** 在 Phase 1 类型层之上加 skeleton class:

- \`src/main/extension/extensionRegistry.ts\` —— 单一只读视图,把现有 PluginRegistry + SkillDiscoveryService 投影成 \`AgentExtension[]\`

  - \`getExtensions()\` 唯一方法,确定性排序(source 字典序 → id 字典序)
  - \`getExtensionRegistry()\` lazy 单例,委托给 \`getPluginRegistry()\` + \`getSkillDiscoveryService()\`
  - \`resetExtensionRegistry()\` 测试钩

旧 \`PluginRegistry\` / \`SkillDiscoveryService\` 一行没动,**没有任何消费方在使用 ExtensionRegistry**。

## 设计要点

| 决策 | 理由 |
|---|---|
| Constructor 注入 minimum interface | 测试不必构造真 PluginRegistry / SkillDiscoveryService;Phase 3 灰度场景可注入自定义实现 |
| 不持有状态 | plugins / skills 都是 in-memory 单例,读取廉价;cache 会带来过期问题,不值得 |
| 确定性排序(source → id) | 让 cache key / snapshot diff 稳定;未来用作 tool 列表时让 LLM prompt cache 命中 |
| 同 id 两侧都出现 → 两条都返回 | Phase 2 不引入合并语义,留给 Phase 3 决策;消费方现在没人,不会撞 |

builtin plugin 用 \`rootPath\` 的 \`builtin:\` 前缀推断 source='builtin',第三方 → source='plugin'(沿用现有 plugin 系统的 rootPath 占位符约定)。

## 测试(12 cases,全 pass)

\`tests/unit/extension/extensionRegistry.test.ts\`:
- 空 sources / 只 plugins / 只 skills / 混合
- builtin vs 第三方 rootPath 推断

- 排序确定性:builtin → cloud → library → plugin → project → user,同 source 内 id 字典序
- 同 id 在两侧都出现 → 两条都返回(plugin + user 双 source)
- mock minimum interface 即可(验证解耦)
- 同 sources 多次调用 → 输出相等(纯函数)
- plugin 完整字段(version/author/capabilities/platforms)投影正确

加上 Phase 1 的 17 cases,extension/ 累计 29/29 pass,\`npm run typecheck\` 干净。
